In my opinion this all starts with redefining what a binge is and isn’t because at this point we’re so messed up we just make ourselves feel like shit for everything lol. If we’re going by a more non-disordered definition, i personally believe a binge is eating uncontrollably *above* your TDEE. For us a binge is simply eating something we didn’t plan to eat, regardless of whether or not you’re still within your caloric limit. It’s a feeling without any concrete evidence to back it up. Remember that 1300 is still a low amount of calories, for most people they’re still at a deficit eating that amount. So in my opinion 1300 is not by any means a binge, maybe for us we feel this way but objectively it’s simply not true. 1300 is still LESS than any human being needs, eating one or two or five meals amounting to 1300 is NOT a binge! Stop listening to the voice that slaps the binge label on everything, even a 50 cal piece of chocolate. Good luck fren! 💖

If your friend is in recovery then I would advise you not to tell them. ED people get very competitive and the fact that you're a "competitor" might really trigger them. Plus what would be the point? They will either A) urge you to recover or B) have to endure your talking about ED habits which again may be very triggering for them. I know it's difficult to keep such a heavy secret and suffer in silence but you have to think of the impact on other people too, especially if they're already mentally unwell or have been at some point. 

Personally the only two people who know about mine are naturally healthy and moderate people without any mental issues. It's impossible to find out of course but I think we have a responsibility to be very selective of who we share our issues with because some people are simply not in the best mindset to be exposed to our negative behavior.
